_notes: Post-reset layout 2026-08-22 (evening). Two roster bugs that froze this file are FIXED and
green: (1) run-roster --loop no longer relaunches a rate-limited model fresh every cycle —
a deferred spec cools off per-spec and RESUMES in place, with a 10m cycle gap, so no more
3x/min hammering; (2) the session account is now harness-bound (runner/SDK) — the model no
longer sees or passes an account, so a lane can no longer land on the wrong one by omission.
Worldserver is up and healthy on the reclaim image; NO rebuild was needed for either fix.
Safe to launch once the operator confirms.
The fleet is this file. One lane = one sequential episode stream = one game account;
parallelism is exactly the number of enabled lanes. Edit while run-fleet is up: it
re-reads every 60s. enabled:false drains a lane (its roster process is SIGTERMed at
the next episode boundary — the running episode finishes); enabled:true or a new
lane spawns one. A malformed edit never kills running lanes: the fleet complains and
keeps the last good config.
Lane policy: OpenCode Zen and OpenRouter lanes carry FREE models only. One stream
per MODEL config: a model appears in at most one lane, so no single model pool is
ever hit concurrently. Several lanes may share a provider (they share that API
key's account-wide rate limits — the adapter's 429/backoff handling is what keeps
that polite; if a provider starts daily-capping, disable lanes rather than retry
harder). claude models run ONLY via the claude-subscription driver, never through
an openai-driver lane.
Entries use the exact per-entry schema of roster JSONs (model, driver, effort,
character, race, class, episodeMs, ...). account comes from the lane. A lane may
point at a rosterFile instead of inline entries. Run ids derive as
fleet-<lane>-<model-slug>[-<effort>]-<date> so fleet runs never collide with
hand-launched rosters.
sub-opus is the burn switch: flip it to true when there is subscription budget to
burn, back to false to stop after the episode in flight.
Model curation (2026-08-22 evening, from provider-body evidence): openai/gpt-oss-20b:free
pruned as genuinely no-longer-free (provider 404 'use the paid slug openai/gpt-oss-20b';
paid slug is a separate free-only-lane-policy decision). gemma-4-31b dropped too — tapped
out, 0 turns all day, same upstream-pool saturation as glm. Added four fresh capable free
OpenRouter models (verified 0/0 pricing 2026-08-22): thinkingmachines/inkling:free and
nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free (large agentic MoEs), cohere/north-mini-code:free
(agentic coding), dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free (512k ctx). glm-5.2 kept as a tail
filler; mimo/deepseek stay (recoverable upstream-pool 429s, not payment errors). The loop
fix keeps any saturated model from hammering.
ox-alpha lane: stealth/ox-alpha is the model that PASSED the Phase 0 gate (gate2-ox-4).
It fell out of the fleet when the fleet became the launch path. Still live and free on
OpenRouter (verified 2026-08-22, pricing 0/0). Given the ~1-week stealth window it gets
its own account (RUNNER) and a solo lane for clean continuous data — do not pad it.
Local lanes: an openai lane may point apiBase at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible
endpoint (e.g. LM Studio on the LAN). That is NOT a shared free-cloud pool, so it
is exempt from the free-model-suffix rule — but the claude bar still holds: no
claude-* id ever rides an openai lane. Its apiKeyEnv (LMSTUDIO_KEY) is a dummy the
server ignores; the pipeline just needs the var to exist in .env.
